clauses.clause: (1) clinical judgment outside the software; never diagnose, issue/suggest/validate clearance or document, prescribe against a known restriction
clauses.founderSource: D2.3: 'nenhum diagnóstico; nenhuma liberação médica fictícia; nenhum exercício contrário a uma contraindicação conhecida.' B3: 'Não tratar uma simples declaração do usuário como liberação médica emitida pelo software. Não permitir que uma contraindicação conhecida seja ignorada.' (G1/§1 left column: 'nunca emite nem sugere liberação médica, nunca valida documento')

clauses.clause: (2) Situation 1: the five reports, 3-14 days, per affected sport, four intents, engine sets the dose
clauses.founderSource: B1: 'O usuário deve conseguir comunicar: Indisposição leve. Fadiga acima do habitual. Doença leve. Pequenos desconfortos. Necessidade de descansar temporariamente. O sistema deve permitir redução temporária por 3 a 14 dias.' D2.1 row 1: 'reduzir a dificuldade; só atividades leves compatíveis; reduzir bastante as sessões; ou descansar.'
clauses.issue: The four intents are renamed. 'Light reduction' is not 'reduzir a dificuldade': D1.4 names difficulty as its own axis ('os controles independentes de volume e de dificuldade'), so the rename loses the axis the Founder chose. 'Substantial reduction' drops 'as sessões'; 'light activity only' drops 'compatíveis'.

clauses.clause: (3) Situation 2: professional-assessment recommendation without diagnosis; structured readiness declaration with current clear screen opens a conservative per-sport restart; never a clearance; no certificate upload required
clauses.founderSource: D2.1 row 2: 'O produto recomenda avaliação profissional, sem diagnosticar. Quando o atleta informa que se recuperou e está pronto, há um caminho utilizável de recomeço esportivo, sem upload universal de atestado. A declaração do atleta nunca é apresentada como liberação médica emitida pelo app. Restrições existentes e sinais relevantes não são ignorados.' B3: 'Não exigir universalmente upload de atestado.' G1: 'com triagem atual ... recomeço esportivo conservador, que não é liberação'.
clauses.note: 'No certificate upload is required' is within B3 ('not universally'). It is not a Founder ban on any case-specific or optional upload; that question stays with the Founder (already routed by the author).

clauses.clause: (4) Situation 3: new plan from updated assessment; after a clinical hold only once readiness is declared
clauses.founderSource: D2.1 row 3: 'Novo plano, com avaliação atualizada de objetivos, experiência recente, capacidade e disponibilidade.' The 'after a clinical hold, only with readiness' part is a protective inference (prevents the onboarding bypass the earlier P-3 forbade); it narrows, never widens.

clauses.clause: (5) Return: gradual at chosen speed, within engine limits, never restoring prior loads or paces automatically; speeds are not the coach profiles
clauses.founderSource: D2.1 row 1: 'Depois, a retomada é gradual, no ritmo conservador, equilibrado ou mais rápido, sempre dentro das regras de segurança do motor.' D2.2: 'a preferência de velocidade de retomada não substitui os limites seguros do motor; os três perfis permanentes de treinador não são as três velocidades temporárias de retomada.' B2: 'Uma retomada mais rápida não é autorização para restaurar automaticamente cargas e ritmos anteriores.' D2.1 row 3: 'Cargas e ritmos antigos não voltam sem evidência.'
clauses.issue: D2 attaches the three speeds to Situation 1; (5) applies them to every return, while (3) calls the post-hold restart 'conservative'. See flagged point 4 for 'automatically'.

clauses.clause: (6) 'Running and strength are judged separately: one can be reduced or held without suspending the other.'
clauses.founderSource: D2.2: 'corrida e força são consideradas juntas; uma modalidade pode ser reduzida sem suspender a outra.' D1.4 preserves 'planejamento híbrido e adaptação entre modalidades'.
clauses.issue: The Founder's first bullet ('considered together', the hybrid differentiator) is dropped and replaced by its opposite framing. The per-sport hold half is faithful. Wording defect only; the fix needs no Founder decision.

clauses.clause: (7) history, records, prior capacity, episodes and decisions preserved; R-F08-1
clauses.founderSource: D2.1 row 3: 'Histórico, recordes e conquistas são preservados.'

clauses.clause: Scope column: partial supersession of DR-99
clauses.issue: (a) 'suspected illness' is SSCTR-05's phrase (cited from DR-99's scope column), not DR-99 row text; the record JSON says 'through SSCTR-05', the DR text does not. (b) The supersession list omits the restriction-end rule (flagged point 2), which touches DR-99 'contraindications ... stay CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED' and AEC 'Restrição declarada: resolução pelo responsável competente'; with 'The rest of DR-99 stands', protection 3 and DR-99 read as contradictory.

clauses.issue: Protection 3 says 'until the person states that it ended' without 'structured'; the author's own reading (RC-09) requires a structured statement, and free text must never end a restriction.

flaggedPoints.subject: Q4: MILD_ILLNESS is a Situation 1 fact of its own; while it stands the `illness` question asks about another or worse illness
flaggedPoints.founderSource: B1: 'Doença leve.' ... 'O sistema deve permitir redução temporária por 3 a 14 dias.' D2.1 row 1. Against: DR-99/SSCTR-05 'suspected illness ... CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED' and §1 left column 'Sinal atual relevante (dor, doença, ...) leva à recomendação de avaliação profissional'. The later, specific Founder words (B1) prevail narrowly (PCG-V1CP-F01).
conditions: The scoping is a Founder-decided narrowing of the `illness` question for the reported condition. RF-1's sentence 'not a relaxation of any screen' is inaccurate and must say so honestly (TC-10).

For the scoped condition, the warning-sign instrument is the only screen left; the SSCTR must state which items detect a mild illness turning relevant (worsening, systemic signs, persistence past the window).
`illness: true` stays clinical at every decision; no conversion between channels; no chaining past 14 days (RC-06, RC-07).

subpoints.subject: MINOR_DISCOMFORT against `pain`
subpoints.classification: PCG extension (INFERRED from B1 by the same necessity as Q4), not Founder wording.
conditions: `persistentPain` is never scoped; pain with a substitution routes clinical.
A discomfort still present at the window's end, or recurring, is not re-windowed without an SSCTR rule and is asked against `persistentPain`.
The instrument covers pain that changes movement and swelling (as the author states); the SSCTR confirms.

subpoints.subject: readiness 'current screen' asks about signs other than or worse than what the declaration carries
subpoints.founderSource: D2.2: 'uma modalidade pode ser reduzida sem suspender a outra.' D2.1 row 2: 'Restrições existentes e sinais relevantes não são ignorados.' §1 right column: 'Suspender as duas modalidades quando a restrição é de uma só' is excessive.
subpoints.issue: As written, the scoping could cover a warning-sign item or a systemic sign the declaration 'carries' (for example a sport declared not ready because of chest pain), letting the other sport restart with a warning sign current. That would weaken a clinical protection.

flaggedPoints.subject: A restriction ends only when the athlete states, in a structured way, that it ended
flaggedPoints.founderSource: §1 left column (Chief-prepared, adopted by D2.6 as the indispensable protections): 'Contraindicação ou restrição conhecida limita a prescrição até o atleta informar que acabou.' Founder words that bound it: D2.3 'nenhum exercício contrário a uma contraindicação conhecida'; B3 'Não permitir que uma contraindicação conhecida seja ignorada'; D2.1 row 2 (recovery declared by the athlete, no universal certificate); D2 closing line 'nem bloqueio permanente nem ausência de segurança'.
flaggedPoints.classification: INFERRED from D2 through the adopted §1; 'structured' is a protective addition of the author.
conditions: The normative texts (DR-148 protection 3, AEC overlay) must say 'structured' (TC-8); free text, time, training, silence or a score never end a restriction.
The end statement is append-only, forward-only, scope-bound and accompanied by a current screen; the restricted scope restarts by the restart rules, never at prior loads (RC-09).
The supersession of DR-99 'contraindications' and of the AEC 'Restrição declarada' exit owner must be explicit (TC-3).
flaggedPoints.founderVisibility: Non-blocking: in-product, a restriction a professional set now ends on the athlete's own structured statement. This follows D2, but the Founder should see it stated in the closure summary.

flaggedPoints.subject: G4 transfer of triage (warning-sign screen) to SSCTR nonclinical scope, its extension to the Situation 1 entry screen, and RF-1 to RF-8
flaggedPoints.founderSource: G4 (adopted by D2.6) for the readiness path. For the extension: B1 (mild illness and minor discomfort must reach the reduction), B3 ('Não permitir que uma contraindicação conhecida seja ignorada'), B6 ('Não declarar F08 concluído enquanto existir uma situação comum de recuperação na qual o usuário não consiga legitimamente voltar a treinar'), D2.1 row 1 ('sempre dentro das regras de segurança do motor'), §1 left column ('Sinal atual relevante ... a qualquer momento').
flaggedPoints.reasoning: Readiness path: within G4 and necessary under D2.5/B6. Extension: without a screen B1 cannot separate mild from relevant, and with G04 as owner (none exists) Situation 1 would stay blocked against B6; the extension is a necessary consequence, labelled as the author's reading R-2 (INFERRED), not Founder wording. The 'not G04 approval, not medical screening' wording mirrors SSCTR-05 ('not service-model legal approval or medical screening').
flaggedPoints.rfAdmissibility: RF-1 to RF-8 are admissible and protective (additive only; each item answered; unknown is ASK; any yes routes the clinical hold; all-no is never 'safe'; narrowing is a re-review trigger; same or stricter instrument during S2w and S6; urgency stays G04).
conditions: G04 column 4 must carry the Situation 1 exception too (TC-6).
Urgency wording (PCG-V1CP-F03) stays with the Founder for interim acceptance; it blocks final copy.
The earlier T2 text said 'with legal review'; that review is not performed here and stays routed to D1.5 (Founder with legal support). Record it as routed, not done.

flaggedPoints.subject: PCG-V1CP-F02: 'automatically' read as 'by date or elapsed time alone'
flaggedPoints.founderSource: B2: 'Uma retomada mais rápida não é autorização para restaurar automaticamente cargas e ritmos anteriores.' D2.1 row 3: 'Cargas e ritmos antigos não voltam sem evidência.' D2.1 row 1: 'a retomada é gradual, no ritmo conservador, equilibrado ou mais rápido'. D2.2: 'a preferência de velocidade de retomada não substitui os limites seguros do motor'.
flaggedPoints.ruling: The text supports 'automatically' = without evidence: D2.1 row 3 sets evidence as the contrast. B2 also says the faster choice itself is no authorization, so the speed choice is never evidence. 'Never in one step' is not B2's wording. But D2.1 row 1 makes the return gradual at every speed, faster included, and the author's reading I-V1CP-2 and RC-12 leave 'gradual' out.
flaggedPoints.founderClarificationNeeded: Only if the SSCTR keeps a FASTER row that returns to the full prior dose at the first post-window session: DESIGN 'Resume the held state: the pre-window doses' (after REDUCE_LIGHT/REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL) and SHORT 'resume the last completed doses'. Those restore prior doses at a date (the window's end) with no executed evidence at that dose, which fails even the author's reading unless the SSCTR shows the executed reduced-dose window or the existing approved SHORT recipe is that evidence. Question for the Founder: does 'gradual' admit a faster return that reaches the pre-window dose in one step after a short window?
